d31b65bba8.why: Old T1 problem fixed: the question no longer asks 'the heart pumps blood round'; it asks what Harvey's sums showed against Galen. In chapter 9 Harvey reckons that the heart sends out more than the whole body contains in half an hour, more than the food eaten could supply. The wrong choices avoid his own true arguments (vessels bursting; the body unable to hold it). Every 'makes blood from food' choice fails on the same sums, so following the reasoning decides it. No arithmetic asked; no date opens the stem; Galen 129-c.216, Greek, of the Roman Empire.

7c1df58cf6.why: Context fixed: Fabricius 'described and drew' the valves (De venarum ostiolis, 1603). Linda Hall says they had been noticed several times before, that Harvey was his pupil, and that Harvey used them to show venous blood flows only toward the heart. The stem and key match Harvey's chapter 13: blood can be pressed up past a valve, but not down toward the hand.

b8fa54f79f.why: Old cross-question giveaway fixed: no vein rule, no right ventricle (so 932af91502's key is safe too), and the context names no direction. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs (Grokipedia). The new wrong choices are the arteries-carry-rich-blood misconception (M1), blood from the lungs (a two-loop mix-up) and mixing (the septum prevents it). The 'artery' trap makes it this grade's fact. Clinical tone.

1d00b74dea.why: Old T1 re-ask fixed: the stem says where the exchange happens and asks why there. Key true: the wall is a single layer of flattened endothelial cells. Valves belong to veins; flow is slowest in capillaries (OpenStax: 30 cm/s in the aorta against 0.026 cm/s, about a thousandth); arterial blood is the richest in oxygen. Malpighi, 1661, frog lung, early compound microscope (Grokipedia).

7a644fabe7.why: Old problems fixed: this is no longer the early-grade 'heart pumps more', and there are no adult litres on the girl. The four choices are parallel organs. Exercise cuts kidney and gut flow by up to 75%, cerebral flow rises about 20-50%, coronary flow can rise four- to five-fold, and the lungs take the right ventricle's whole output, so the kidneys are the only one that loses. 'Three or four times' sits within adult figures of up to 5-6 times. This is how systems work together, reasoned out, at the top of the grade's reach. Clinical tone.
